current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: 113th General Assembly 2nd session (2024) and 114th General Assembly 1st session + 1st extraordinary session (2025) via the OORC Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 Legislative Updates (official) — neither reports any amendment to the fee, estimate, prepayment or nonpayment provisions of Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7) or to § 8-4-604 (2024: PC 1030 open-meetings costs, exemptions; 2025: PC 392 made the disruptive-request injunction permanent, PC 360 agendas, PC 415 ethics-commission records). 2026 session (114th GA 2nd session): no fee amendment located by search; the OORC Fall 2026 update is not yet published — treat as requiring manual verification. Codified availability: the official Tennessee Code Annotated is hosted on Lexis (JavaScript-only) and could not be opened by the tooling; statute text was taken verbatim from FindLaw's reproduction of the TCA (current through Jan. 2, 2024) and every quoted clause was cross-checked against official OORC pages (FAQ, MTAS/CTAS reproductions) that quote the same language. Statute-based rows therefore carry a manual_verification flag. Guidance-vs-law: TN's fee figures live entirely in OORC 'policies and guidelines' (Schedule of Reasonable Charges, Frequent & Multiple Requests policy, Safe Harbor, Model Policy, Best Practices — all effective Jan. 20, 2017; Model Policy amended Aug. 16, 2017), which § 8-4-604(c) says are NOT rules under the UAPA and § 8-4-604(a)(1)(A) calls a guideline a custodian 'may use'. The Schedule has not been revised since 2017 despite § 8-4-604(a)(1)(B) ('revised at least annually'). Consequently the per-page figures are safe-harbor ceilings with a documented-actual-cost escape (Schedule § II.C), not hard statutory caps; the binding statutory standard is 'reasonable costs incurred in producing the requested material' (§ 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)(i)). Municipal scope: § 10-7-503(g)(1) requires county and municipal entities to adopt a written policy stating fees and billing/payment procedures; state agencies instead promulgate UAPA rules under (g)(2) (e.g., Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 1720-01-11-.05, 0240-06-05-.06) — a separate regime not opened here.

OORC Schedule figures bind every 'records custodian'/'governmental entity' subject to the TPRA (state, county and municipal); the schedule is a guideline a custodian 'may use' (§ 8-4-604(a)(1)(A)) and charges must be adopted in the local policy (§ 10-7-503(g)(1)(C)); exceeding the schedule requires documented actual cost (Schedule § II.C) and forfeits the safe-harbor presumption.

resolutions.value: “hourly wage of an employee” — base salary, excluding benefits (annual salary ÷ required hours/year if salaried)
resolutions.unit: USD per hour, computed per employee
resolutions.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § IV.A–E
resolutions.source_language: “Labor” is the time (in hours) reasonably necessary to produce requested records, including the time spent locating, retrieving, reviewing, redacting, and reproducing records. “Hourly wage of an employee” is based upon the base salary of the employee and does not include benefits. If an employee is not paid on an hourly basis, the hourly wage shall be determined by dividing the employee's annual salary by the required hours to be worked per year. For example, an employee who is expected to work a 37.5 hour workweek and receives $39,000 in salary on an annual basis will be deemed to be paid $20 per hour. In calculating labor charges, a records custodian should determine the total amount of labor for each employee and subtract the labor threshold from the labor of the highest paid employee(s). The records custodian should then multiply the amount of labor for each employee by each employee's hourly wage to calculate the total amount of labor charges associated with the request.
resolutions.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017 (submitted to ACOG Nov. 8, 2016). Verified still posted as the operative schedule on the OORC Policies, Guidelines & Forms page as of 2026-08-19; no revision published despite § 8-4-604(a)(1)(B) 'revised at least annually'.
resolutions.notes: Rate is not a number: it is the actual base hourly wage (excl. benefits) of each employee reasonably necessary, using the lowest practicable wage (§ IV.A), charged only above the labor threshold (≥1 hour, § IV.C) and only for producing copies (never inspection, § I.A / § 10-7-503(a)(7)(A)(i)). Same computed standard for search, review/redaction and reproduction — § IV.B lists 'locating, retrieving, reviewing, redacting, and reproducing'. Locating/retrieving = search.

It is presumed copies of requested records will be provided in person to a requestor when the requestor returns to the records custodian's office to retrieve the records. D. If a requestor chooses not to personally retrieve records and the actual cost of delivering the copies, in addition to any other permitted charges, have been paid by the requestor or otherwise waived pursuant to the public records policy, then a records custodian is obligated to deliver the copies via USPS First-Class Mail. It is within the discretion of a records custodian to agree to deliver copies of records through other means, including electronically, and to assess the costs related to such delivery.
new_rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § III.C–D
new_rules.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017 (submitted to ACOG Nov. 8, 2016). Verified still posted as the operative schedule on the OORC Policies, Guidelines & Forms page as of 2026-08-19; no revision published despite § 8-4-604(a)(1)(B) 'revised at least annually'.
new_rules.notes: Actual cost of delivery (postage) — no fixed handling fee. OORC FAQ (official): a requestor cannot be required to retrieve in person; 'the governmental entity is required to mail the records after receiving payment for the cost of delivering the public records.' § 8-4-604(a)(1)(A)(i) directs the schedule to consider 'the costs of mailing the documents if the requestor is not returning to retrieve the requested documents.'

new_rules.legal_concept: Electronic records: per-page charge only when new paper copies had to be produced (e.g., printed to redact)
new_rules.atomic_rule: When providing electronic records, a records custodian may charge per-page costs only when paper copies that did not already exist had to be produced in responding to the request, such as when a record must be printed to be redacted.
new_rules.trigger: Records requested/produced in electronic form.
new_rules.source_language: When providing electronic records, a records custodian may charge per-page costs only when paper copies that did not already exist are required to be produced in responding to the request, such as when a record must be printed to be redacted.
new_rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § III.B (second sentence)
new_rules.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017 (submitted to ACOG Nov. 8, 2016). Verified still posted as the operative schedule on the OORC Policies, Guidelines & Forms page as of 2026-08-19; no revision published despite § 8-4-604(a)(1)(B) 'revised at least annually'.
new_rules.notes: OORC FAQ (official) restates: for copies of electronic records an entity 'may only assess a per-page charge for paper copies that must be produced ... labor charges ... and its out-of-pocket costs for flash drives or other storage devices'; no charge may be assessed for inspecting electronic records.

new_rules.legal_concept: No charge to view/inspect a public record unless otherwise required by law
new_rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity shall not assess a charge to view a public record unless otherwise required by law; therefore copy and labor charges attach only to requests for copies.
new_rules.trigger: Request to inspect/view (as opposed to copy).
new_rules.source_language: (7)(A)(i) A governmental entity shall not require a written request or assess a charge to view a public record unless otherwise required by law.
new_rules.source_authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(A)(i); OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.A ('Records custodians may not charge for inspection of public records except as provided by law.')
new_rules.effective_status: Current (FindLaw reproduction current through Jan. 2, 2024; OORC 2024 and 2025 Legislative Updates report no amendment to these provisions; 2026 session: no fee amendment found, OORC Fall 2026 update not yet published)
new_rules.notes: Bounds WHEN labor is chargeable: only in producing copies (Schedule § IV.B 'labor' = time to produce requested records). OORC FAQ: if a copy request is converted to inspection-only, no inspection-related costs may be charged; a staff member sitting with an inspecting requestor may not be charged for. Confirm against the official TCA before library entry.

new_rules.legal_concept: OORC schedule is a guideline a custodian 'may use'; OORC policies are not UAPA rules
new_rules.atomic_rule: The Office of Open Records Counsel shall establish a schedule of reasonable charges that a records custodian may use as a guideline to charge a citizen requesting copies; the schedule shall be revised at least annually; the OORC policies and guidelines are not rules under the Uniform Administrative Procedures Act.
new_rules.trigger: Custodian sets copy charges under § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)(i).
new_rules.source_language: (a) The office of open records counsel shall establish: (1)(A) A schedule of reasonable charges that a records custodian may use as a guideline to charge a citizen requesting copies of public records pursuant to title 10, chapter 7, part 5. ... (B) The schedule established pursuant to subdivision (a)(1)(A) shall be revised at least annually; (2) A separate policy related to reasonable charges that a records custodian may charge for frequent and multiple requests for public records; (3) A safe harbor policy for a records custodian who adheres to the policies and guidelines established by the office of open records counsel; ... (c) The policies and guidelines shall not be deemed to be rules under the Uniform Administrative Procedures Act, compiled in title 4, chapter 5.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (FindLaw reproduction current through Jan. 2, 2024; OORC 2024 and 2025 Legislative Updates report no amendment to these provisions; 2026 session: no fee amendment found, OORC Fall 2026 update not yet published)
new_rules.notes: This is the delegation the fee figures flow through: § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)(i) → § 8-4-604 → OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges. Because the schedule is a 'guideline' with a documented-actual-cost escape (Schedule § II.C), its per-page figures are safe-harbor ceilings rather than hard statutory caps. Statute text taken verbatim from FindLaw's reproduction of Tenn. Code Ann. (current through Jan. 2, 2024); the official Lexis-hosted TCA could not be opened by the research tooling. Currency cross-checked against OORC Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 Legislative Updates (no amendment to the fee/estimate/payment provisions of § 10-7-503 in the 2024 or 2025 sessions) and the OORC FAQ (official) which quotes the same clauses. Confirm against the official TCA before library entry.

new_rules.legal_concept: Safe harbor: fees per adopted policy consistent with the OORC Schedule are presumed reasonable
new_rules.atomic_rule: Labor fees and copy charges are presumed reasonable if set forth in the entity's public records policy and developed in accordance with the OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges; aggregation charges likewise if developed under the Frequent and Multiple Requests policy.
new_rules.trigger: Entity charges fees under an adopted policy consistent with OORC guidelines.
new_rules.source_language: Any labor fees and charges related to copying or duplicating public records are presumed reasonable if the fees and charges are set forth in the governmental entity's public records policy and such fees and charges were developed in accordance with the provisions of the Schedule of Reasonable Charges. The aggregation of frequent and multiple requests for copies of public records and any fees and charges resulting from aggregation are presumed to be reasonable if the fees and charges are set forth in the governmental entity's public records policy and such fees and charges were developed in accordance with the provisions of the Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests Policy.
new_rules.source_authority: OORC Safe Harbor Policy (Tenn. Code Ann. § 8-4-604(a)(3))
new_rules.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017
new_rules.notes: Explains why the schedule's 'up to' figures operate as ceilings for practical purposes: exceeding them forfeits the presumption unless actual cost is documented (Schedule § II.C).

new_rules.legal_concept: Commercial-value GIS/geographic data: additional development-cost recovery fee capped at 10% (10–20% with approvals); not chargeable to individuals for themselves; news media at reproduction cost
new_rules.atomic_rule: For a copy request for a public record that has commercial value and requires reproduction of a publicly funded computer-generated map or similar geographic data, a state agency or political subdivision may impose reasonable additional fees tied to actual development costs, limited to 10% of total development costs (10–20% only with governing-body and ISC approval); such fees may not be assessed against individuals requesting for themselves or when the record lacks commercial value; news media may be charged cost of reproduction only.
new_rules.trigger: Copy request for commercial-value GIS/geographic data developed with public funds.
new_rules.source_language: (c)(1) If a request is made for a copy of a public record that has commercial value, and such request requires the reproduction of all or a portion of a computer generated map or other similar geographic data that was developed with public funds, a state department or agency or a political subdivision of the state having primary responsibility for the data or system may establish and impose reasonable fees for the reproduction of such record, in addition to any fees or charges that may lawfully be imposed pursuant to this section. The additional fees authorized by this subsection (c) may not be assessed against individuals who request copies of records for themselves or when the record requested does not have commercial value. State departments and agencies and political subdivisions of the state may charge a reasonable fee (cost of reproduction only) for information requested by the news media for news gathering purposes (broadcast or publication). ... (3) The development cost recovery set forth above shall be limited to not more than ten percent (10%) of the total development costs unless additional development cost recovery between ten percent (10%) and twenty percent (20%) is approved by the following procedures: ... For political subdivisions of the state, approval for additional development cost recovery as contained in a proposed business plan must be obtained from the governing legislative body. If the governing legislative body approves additional development cost recovery, such recovery shall be submitted to the ISC for approval. ... (4) As used in this subsection (c), "record that has commercial value" means a record requested for any purpose other than: (A) A non-business use by an individual; and (B) A news gathering use by the news media.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (FindLaw reproduction current through Jan. 2, 2024; OORC 2024 and 2025 Legislative Updates report no amendment to these provisions; 2026 session: no fee amendment found, OORC Fall 2026 update not yet published)
new_rules.notes: AMENDS TN-0049 (which flagged § 10-7-506(c) as unopened): the enumerated fee is confined to commercial-value GIS/geographic-data reproductions; there is no general commercial-purpose surcharge and standard copy/labor charges do not vary by purpose (Schedule § I.F). Recovery of maintenance costs is not subject to the 10%/20% limits. Statute text taken verbatim from FindLaw's reproduction of Tenn. Code Ann. (current through Jan. 2, 2024); the official Lexis-hosted TCA could not be opened by the research tooling. Currency cross-checked against OORC Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 Legislative Updates (no amendment to the fee/estimate/payment provisions of § 10-7-503 in the 2024 or 2025 sessions) and the OORC FAQ (official) which quotes the same clauses. Confirm against the official TCA before library entry.

new_rules.legal_concept: Municipal policy must state fees for copies and billing/payment procedures
new_rules.atomic_rule: Every county and municipal governmental entity must have a written public records policy adopted by its governing authority that includes a statement of any fees charged for copies and the procedures for billing and payment, and must not impose requirements more burdensome than state law.
new_rules.trigger: Entity subject to § 10-7-503 (county/municipal).
new_rules.source_language: (g)(1) No later than July 1, 2018, every county and municipal governmental entity subject to this section shall establish a written public records policy properly adopted by the appropriate governing authority. The public records policy shall not impose requirements on those requesting records that are more burdensome than state law and shall include: ... (C) A statement of any fees charged for copies of public records and the procedures for billing and payment; ...
new_rules.source_authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(g)(1)(C)
new_rules.effective_status: Current (FindLaw reproduction current through Jan. 2, 2024; OORC 2024 and 2025 Legislative Updates report no amendment to these provisions; 2026 session: no fee amendment found, OORC Fall 2026 update not yet published)
new_rules.notes: The statutory hook for every 'defers_to_city' resolution in this pass: fee amounts, waiver, prepayment thresholds, payment forms and aggregation are set in the locally adopted policy (Schedule § I.B: 'Charges for copies of public records must be pursuant to a public records policy properly adopted by the governing authority'). State agencies instead promulgate UAPA rules under (g)(2) — a separate regime. Statute text taken verbatim from FindLaw's reproduction of Tenn. Code Ann. (current through Jan. 2, 2024); the official Lexis-hosted TCA could not be opened by the research tooling. Currency cross-checked against OORC Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 Legislative Updates (no amendment to the fee/estimate/payment provisions of § 10-7-503 in the 2024 or 2025 sessions) and the OORC FAQ (official) which quotes the same clauses. Confirm against the official TCA before library entry.

new_rules.legal_concept: No charge may be collected until an estimate of reasonable charges has been provided
new_rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may not charge for the costs of providing copies until an estimate of reasonable charges has been provided to the requestor.
new_rules.trigger: Copies produced/charges assessed without a prior estimate.
new_rules.source_language: A governmental entity may not charge for the costs associated with providing copies of public records until an estimate of reasonable charges is provided to the requestor.
new_rules.source_authority: OORC Tennessee Public Records Act FAQs, 'What if a governmental entity does not provide an estimate of costs?' (applying Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)(ii))
new_rules.effective_status: Current (OORC FAQ page, no revision date shown; opened 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: Guidance interpretation of the statutory estimate duty; combined with § 10-7-503(a)(7)(A)(vii)(b) (bar applies only where the requestor 'agreed to pay the estimated cost'), an overrun beyond the agreed estimate is not covered by the nonpayment bar. No explicit revised-estimate rule exists.

new_rules.legal_concept: Notice of aggregation and right to appeal to OORC when threshold met
new_rules.atomic_rule: When the aggregation threshold is met, a custodian choosing to aggregate must inform the requestor(s) of the determination and of their right to appeal the decision to the OORC; disputes regarding aggregation are brought to the OORC.
new_rules.trigger: Aggregation threshold reached and custodian elects to aggregate.
new_rules.source_language: B. When the aggregation threshold is met, a records custodian choosing to aggregate requests must inform the requestor(s) of the determination to aggregate and of the right of the requestor(s) to appeal the records custodian's decision to aggregate to the OORC. ... D. Disputes regarding aggregation shall be brought to the OORC.
new_rules.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § II.B, II.D
new_rules.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017
new_rules.notes: Required notice + administrative appeal path (OORC) attached to the aggregation decision.

new_rules.legal_concept: Routinely released, readily accessible records exempt from aggregation
new_rules.atomic_rule: Requests for current records that are routinely released and readily accessible, such as agendas or meeting minutes, are exempt from the aggregation policy.
new_rules.trigger: Request is for routinely released, readily accessible current records.
new_rules.source_language: C. Requests for current records that are routinely released and readily accessible, such as agendas or meeting minutes, are exempt from this policy.
new_rules.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § II.C
new_rules.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017
new_rules.notes: Model Policy § VI.I.2.c has the entity list its excluded routine records.

new_rules.legal_concept: Policy must specify the level (entity / agency / department / office) at which requests are aggregated
new_rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity's public records policy shall specify the level at which records requests will be aggregated — for the entire entity or by agency, department, office, or otherwise.
new_rules.trigger: Entity elects to aggregate.
new_rules.source_language: E. A governmental entity's public record policy shall specify the level at which records requests will be aggregated, whether for the entire governmental entity or by agency, department, office, or otherwise.
new_rules.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § I.E
new_rules.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017
new_rules.notes: Aggregation is optional (policy purpose: 'It is within the discretion of each governmental entity to charge for frequent and multiple record requests').

new_rules.legal_concept: Best practice: full or partial prepayment of estimated charges when duplication costs are significant; segment payment with segmented production; prepay vendor cost
new_rules.atomic_rule: OORC best practice (advisory): an entity should consider requiring full or partial payment of estimated charges before production when duplication costs are significant; where production is segmented, the prepayment requirement should be segmented accordingly; where an outside vendor is used, payment should be required in advance based on the estimated cost.
new_rules.trigger: Significant duplication costs / segmented production / outside vendor.
new_rules.source_language: H. A governmental entity should consider requiring and receiving either full or partial payment of estimated charges prior to production of copies when duplication costs for requested records are significant. I. If a records custodian is going to segment the production of requested records, the requirement for payment prior to the production of the records should also be segmented accordingly. ... J.3. When an outside vendor is utilized, the records custodian should require payment by the requestor in advance based on the estimated cost.
new_rules.source_authority: OORC Best Practices & Guidelines § III.H, III.I, III.J.3
new_rules.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017
new_rules.notes: Advisory ('should') — not a mandate; confirms no state cap on the deposit share (full OR partial permitted).

new_rules.legal_concept: Official response form: unpaid estimated fees is a stated ground for not producing copies
new_rules.atomic_rule: The OORC Records Response Form lists 'You have not paid the estimated copying/production fees' as a ground on which the response to a request is denied (production withheld).
new_rules.trigger: Requestor has not paid the estimated fees where prepayment is required.
new_rules.source_language: You have not paid the estimated copying/production fees.
new_rules.source_authority: OORC Records Request Response Form (form referenced in Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(2)(B)(ii)–(iii))
new_rules.effective_status: Current (version posted on OORC Policies, Guidelines & Forms page as of 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: The form (also embedded in the Model Policy) is how the 7-business-day response is documented; the state specifies no clock effect, grace period or lapse action for an unpaid deposit — the hold simply persists until payment.

new_rules.legal_concept: Best practice: entity should determine administrative cost of charging — a minimum fee may be needed to avoid losing money
new_rules.atomic_rule: OORC best practice (advisory): whether charging for copies or labor, an entity should determine its administrative costs associated with charging fees, as there may be a minimum amount of fees necessary to avoid losing money from processing charges.
new_rules.trigger: Entity designs its fee policy.
new_rules.source_language: G. Whether charging for copies or labor, a governmental entity should determine its administrative costs associated with charging fees as there may be a minimum amount of fees necessary in order to avoid losing money from processing charges.
new_rules.source_authority: OORC Best Practices & Guidelines § III.G
new_rules.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017
new_rules.notes: No state minimum fee; the state expressly leaves any minimum to the entity's own cost analysis.

applicability_notes: OORC Schedule/policies: addressed to every 'records custodian' / 'governmental entity' under the TPRA (state, county, municipal); recorded as all_public_bodies. They are guidelines that become operative only through the entity's adopted policy (§ 10-7-503(g)(1); Schedule § I.B), so every schedule figure is a safe-harbor bound the city adopts at or below, or exceeds with documented actual cost.

§ 10-7-503(g)(1) (policy content incl. fees and billing/payment) binds county and municipal entities; (g)(2) sends state agencies to UAPA rules — agency fee rules (Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs.) were not opened and do not bind cities.
§ 9-1-108(c) (credit/debit acceptance + mandatory pass-through processing fee) applies to 'municipal or county entity or officer' — municipalities yes; state agencies are under different provisions.

§ 10-7-506(c) GIS commercial-value fee applies to 'a state department or agency or a political subdivision of the state' — all public bodies, but only for commercial-value computer-generated maps/geographic data.
The estimate duty, prepayment permission and nonpayment bar in § 10-7-503(a)(7) apply to every governmental entity.
material_negatives: No graduated per-page bands (flat ceilings only; duplex = 2 pages).
No labor time increment or rounding rule (labor 'in hours').
No overhead/fringe multiplier — the schedule affirmatively excludes benefits from the chargeable wage.
No requester response window for estimates, no revision-% trigger, no estimate validity period.
No deposit cap (full or partial prepayment contemplated); no clock effect, grace or lapse action for an unpaid deposit.
No statutory withdrawal-after-N-days for nonpayment — the consequence is a future-request bar until paid.
No certified-copy charge in the TPRA or OORC instruments.
No per-recording / per-minute / free-minutes rule for audio/video.
No general commercial-purpose surcharge (Schedule § I.F) — only the § 10-7-506(c) GIS development-cost fee.
No fee forfeiture for a late response (late/no response = deemed denial with court remedy only).
No repeat-request carry-forward; only aggregation of frequent/multiple requests.
The OORC Schedule has not been revised since Jan. 20, 2017 despite the annual-revision directive in § 8-4-604(a)(1)(B).
